_about: Evaluation dataset for assist-lane retrieval (AM-28 Tier 2). See README.md.
Authored 2026-08-26 against a full read of the actual supplied documents, at the
owner's direction; every ANSWERABLE source clause verified by reading it, every
NOT_FOUND absence verified by search. RATIFIED by the owner on 2026-08-26 by
directing its use for calibration (recorded in AUTO_MODE_DECISIONS #126).
`anchor` is a short cited excerpt (54.6) used ONLY by the harness to locate the
expected chunk mechanically - it is not the answer and never shown to a user.
No document text beyond short cited excerpts (locked 54.6). No counterparty name.

questions.question: Can we walk away from the agreement before it expires, and what would it cost us?
questions.rationale: Customer has no early-termination right; electing to terminate anyway makes the customer liable for the total fees for the remainder of the Term, payable by the termination date.
questions.anchor: early termination fee equal to the total fees

questions.question: Does the agreement renew by itself when the term ends?
questions.rationale: Automatic renewal for successive six-month periods unless either party gives written non-renewal notice at least 30 days before expiry.
questions.anchor: automatically renew for successive periods of six (6) months

questions.question: How much time do we get to fix a breach before the provider can terminate?
questions.rationale: Termination for breach requires the breach to remain uncured 30 days after written notice specifying it.
questions.anchor: cured within thirty (30) days after receipt of written notice

questions.question: What happens to our data once the contract is terminated?
questions.rationale: Customer data is purged from equipment and infrastructure within 15 days of termination, without further notice.
questions.anchor: purge all Customer data

questions.question: If we still owe money after termination, can the provider hold on to our equipment?
questions.rationale: If dues are not settled within 10 days of termination, access can be denied and Customer Equipment retained until full payment.
questions.anchor: retain Customer Equipment until full payment

questions.question: How long do we have to challenge an invoice we think is wrong?
questions.rationale: Invoice disputes must be emailed within 5 working days of receipt; otherwise the invoice is deemed undisputed and payable.
questions.anchor: within 5 working days from the date of receipt of invoice

questions.question: What is the maximum financial exposure of the provider if something goes badly wrong?
questions.rationale: Aggregate liability capped at the amount paid for the specific Services giving rise to the claim in the six months preceding the event.
questions.anchor: six (6) month period immediately preceding

questions.question: Are there situations where the liability cap does not protect the customer side at all?
questions.rationale: The limitations do not apply to the customer's indemnity obligations, payment breaches, or the customer's fraud, wilful misconduct or gross negligence.
questions.anchor: willful misconduct, or gross negligence

questions.question: If a third party sues the provider because of something our users hosted, who pays?
questions.rationale: Customer defends and indemnifies the provider for claims arising from customer content, data, use of the Services, and acts of its users.
questions.anchor: defend, indemnify, and hold harmless

questions.question: If we end up in a dispute, where and how does it get resolved?
questions.rationale: 30 days of informal negotiation, then arbitration by a sole arbitrator (High Court of Mumbai appoints failing consensus) under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act 1996, seat Mumbai, in English.
questions.anchor: High Court of Mumbai

questions.question: If a natural disaster keeps the service down for months, can either side exit?
questions.rationale: A force majeure event continuing beyond 60 consecutive days lets either party terminate on written notice without liability, except amounts already due.
questions.anchor: exceeding sixty (60) consecutive days

questions.question: If we resell the services to our own clients, who is responsible for verifying those end customers?
questions.rationale: The reselling customer is responsible for end-customer KYC and for maintaining compliance records; the provider does not require disclosure of end-customer details.
questions.anchor: KYC verification is completed for those end customers

questions.question: Can we deduct a disputed amount from our next payment to offset a claim we have against the provider?
questions.rationale: All amounts are payable without deduction, set-off or counterclaim, save for TDS.
questions.anchor: without any deduction, set-off or counter claim

questions.question: The commissioned setup is not what we expected. What is our recourse, and how quickly must we act?
questions.rationale: Dissatisfaction upon Commissioning must be notified in writing within 3 days, failing which billing runs from the original Commissioning Date.
questions.anchor: notify LeapSwitch in writing within three (3) days

questions.question: If the provider builds something new while working with us, who owns the intellectual property?
questions.rationale: IP conceived or developed by the provider during or as a result of the relationship remains the provider's sole and exclusive property unless agreed otherwise in writing.
questions.anchor: conceived, made, or developed in whole or in part

questions.question: If our company is acquired, can we transfer this agreement to the acquirer?
questions.rationale: The customer may not assign without prior written consent; the provider may assign at its sole discretion.
questions.anchor: shall not assign any of its rights and obligations

questions.question: If the provider's carelessness causes us losses under the website terms, how much can we actually recover?
questions.rationale: Aggregate liability capped at total fees paid in the twelve months preceding the event; carve-outs for death or personal injury caused by negligence and for fraud.
questions.anchor: TWELVE (12) MONTHS IMMEDIATELY PRECEDING

questions.question: What happens if we pay an invoice late?
questions.rationale: Late fee up to 5% per month after 5 days overdue; suspension possible after 7 days; termination after 30 days; data on terminated services may be permanently deleted.
questions.anchor: late fee/interest of up to 5% per month

questions.question: Which services can we get our money back on if we cancel?
questions.rationale: Web hosting refundable for unused months; domains, dedicated servers, self-managed VPS, firewalls, backup plans, licences and provisioned GPU reservations are not; 30-day money-back only for first-time shared/reseller signups.
questions.anchor: refunded for unused months

questions.question: After we cancel, how long do we have to retrieve our data before it is gone?
questions.rationale: Data is available for retrieval for 7 days after termination, then may be permanently deleted; legally-mandated data is kept for its required period.
questions.anchor: available for retrieval for a period of 7 days

questions.question: Why do we have to complete identity verification before servers are activated, and how is it done?
questions.rationale: KYC is mandated by the CERT-In Direction for Indian datacenter services; via Digio (Aadhaar/DigiLocker or document plus selfie) for Indian customers and Stripe Identity for international ones; services are not provisioned until it completes.
questions.anchor: conducted through Digio

questions.question: How much warning do we get before prices go up?
questions.rationale: At least 30 days' notice of any price increase, taking effect at the next billing cycle; renewal invoices issued at least 7 days before renewal.
questions.anchor: 30 days' notice of any price increase

questions.question: Can we inspect how the provider handles the personal data we host with them?
questions.rationale: Reasonable information about processing and security may be requested; an on-site audit needs 30 days' prior written notice, runs in business hours, at the customer's expense.
questions.anchor: conducted at your expense, during business hours

questions.question: Is submitting a support ticket enough to cancel a service?
questions.rationale: No — cancellation only via the Client Area; ticket or email requests are not accepted, and cancellation takes effect at the end of the billing period.
questions.anchor: Cancellation requests via Support Ticket or email are not accepted

questions.question: What level of availability is promised for a dedicated server, and what do we get if it is missed?
questions.rationale: 99.9% minimum uptime for dedicated servers; credits of 15% (below 99.9% but at least 99%), 40% (below 99% but at least 95%) or 100% (below 95%) of the month's charges for the affected service.
questions.anchor: Commitment to Service Availability

questions.question: Is there a deadline for claiming compensation after an outage?
questions.section: How to Request a Service Credit (1)
questions.rationale: A support request must be submitted within 60 calendar days of the incident; verified credits are issued within 45 days of confirmation, based solely on the provider's monitoring data.
questions.anchor: within sixty (60) calendar days following the incident

questions.question: Beyond service credits, can we recover our business losses from an outage?
questions.section: How to Request a Service Credit (4)
questions.rationale: Service credits are the exclusive remedy for service disruptions and SLA claims, and monthly credits never exceed that month's bill for the affected service.
questions.anchor: exclusive remedy for any service disruptions

questions.question: Does emergency maintenance count against the uptime commitment?
questions.rationale: Emergency maintenance is treated as scheduled maintenance — excluded from availability — provided the customer is informed as soon as possible and the downtime does not exceed 3 hours in the month.
questions.anchor: downtime does not exceed three (3) hours

questions.question: What is the largest service credit the cloud platform will ever pay in a month?
questions.rationale: The credit scale tops out at 20% of the affected service's monthly charge, for uptime below 95%; credits never exceed the monthly charge for the impacted service.
questions.anchor: applicable credit percentage

questions.question: How long do our confidentiality duties continue after the relationship ends?
questions.rationale: Confidentiality obligations survive two years from termination or expiry (whichever is later), and for trade secrets as long as the information remains a trade secret.
questions.anchor: survive for two (2) years from the date of termination

questions.question: Are we allowed to recruit people who work for the Disclosing Party?
questions.rationale: No targeted solicitation of employees, contractors or consultants during the term plus two years; general non-targeted public recruitment advertising is expressly permitted.
questions.anchor: solicit, induce, recruit, or encourage

questions.question: A court orders us to hand over information we received under the NDA. What are we required to do first?
questions.rationale: Promptly notify the Disclosing Party in writing where legally permitted so it can seek protection, and disclose only the legally-required portion.
questions.anchor: seek a protective order

questions.question: If our team simply remembers general know-how from the discussions, can we use it in our business?
questions.rationale: Residuals retained in unaided memory may be used in ordinary business without royalties, but grant no IP licence and do not excuse the reverse-engineering and non-solicitation obligations.
questions.anchor: unaided memory

questions.question: Can we mention the partnership in our marketing or a press release?
questions.rationale: No use of the Disclosing Party's name, logo, brand or the business relationship in any public disclosure without prior written consent.
questions.anchor: press release, public announcement, marketing material

questions.question: Is legal adult content allowed on the hosting services?
questions.rationale: Permitted on dedicated server and VPS lines only, subject to law; not permitted on shared or reseller hosting.
questions.anchor: dedicated server and VPS product lines only

questions.question: What conditions must our marketing emails meet to be acceptable?
questions.rationale: Double opt-in consent with retained evidence (producible within 24 hours on request), valid headers, working unsubscribe, source disclosure, published privacy policy, and CAN-SPAM/ePrivacy compliance.
questions.anchor: double opt-in

questions.question: How is bandwidth overage measured for services sold by Mbps?
questions.rationale: The industry-standard 95th percentile method applies to Mbps-based services unless the service contract specifies otherwise; GB-transfer services are measured on total monthly data.
questions.anchor: 95th percentile

questions.question: How quickly must illegal child-abuse material be taken down, and who gets told?
questions.rationale: Takedown within 2 hours of identification per the 2021 Intermediary Rules as amended; reported to the SJPU or local police and the National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal; account terminated without refund.
questions.anchor: within 2 hours of identification

questions.question: How long does the company keep our billing records after we close our account?
questions.rationale: Account and billing data are retained for the account's duration plus 7 years after closure, per Indian tax law.
questions.anchor: 7 years after account closure

questions.question: If my personal data is exposed in a breach, when will I hear about it and who else is informed?
questions.rationale: CERT-In within 6 hours, the Data Protection Board as required under the DPDPA, and affected individuals without undue delay with consequences and remediation.
questions.anchor: within 6 hours of becoming aware

questions.question: Who do I complain to about how my personal data is handled, and how fast must they respond?
questions.rationale: A designated Grievance Officer acknowledges within 24 hours and endeavours to resolve within 30 days; escalation lies to the Data Protection Board of India.
questions.anchor: acknowledge your grievance within 24 hours

questions.question: Which outside companies get access to my personal data, and for what?
questions.rationale: A named sub-processor table: Cloudflare (CDN/security), Google Analytics, Microsoft Clarity, Tawk.to (chat), HubSpot (marketing), Digio (KYC India), Stripe (payments/KYC international).
questions.anchor: Tawk.to

questions.question: Within what time must a cyber security incident be reported to the national agency?
questions.rationale: Mandatory reporting to CERT-In within 6 hours of noticing an incident or being brought to notice of it.
questions.anchor: within 6 hours of noticing such incidents

questions.question: What are a hosting provider's log-keeping duties under the cyber security directions?
questions.rationale: Logs of all ICT systems must be enabled, kept securely for a rolling 180 days, maintained within Indian jurisdiction, and produced with incident reports or on order.
questions.anchor: rolling period of 180 days

questions.question: What customer information must cloud and VPS providers keep, and for how long after a customer leaves?
questions.rationale: Validated names, period of hire, allotted IPs, registration email/IP/timestamp, purpose of hire, validated address and contacts, and ownership pattern — for at least 5 years after cancellation or withdrawal.
questions.anchor: Ownership pattern of the subscribers

questions.question: What is the penalty for ignoring an information request or direction from the national cyber security agency?
questions.rationale: Imprisonment up to one year, or a fine up to one lakh rupees, or both.
questions.anchor: fails to provide the information called for or comply with the direction

questions.question: Once a refund is approved, how long until we actually receive the money?
questions.rationale: After review and approval, the refund is initiated within 7 working days; the customer must supply bank details and the invoice number to billing.
questions.anchor: within 7 working days after approval

questions.question: Which country's laws govern use of the CloudPe website?
questions.rationale: Matters relating to access or use of the website are governed by the statutes and laws of India and the United States of America, without regard to conflicts principles.
questions.anchor: United States of America, without regard to conflicts

questions.question: What must consent look like for it to be valid under India's data protection law?
questions.rationale: Free, specific, informed, unconditional and unambiguous, given by clear affirmative action, and limited to data necessary for the specified purpose.
questions.anchor: unconditional and unambiguous with a clear affirmative action

questions.question: What is the largest fine for failing to put reasonable security safeguards around personal data?
questions.rationale: A monetary penalty which may extend to two hundred and fifty crore rupees for breach of the section 8(5) security-safeguards obligation.
questions.anchor: two hundred and fifty crore rupees

questions.question: Is a platform allowed to show targeted advertising to children?
questions.rationale: Tracking, behavioural monitoring of children and targeted advertising directed at children are prohibited; processing a child's data needs verifiable parental consent under 9(1).
questions.anchor: targeted advertising directed at children

questions.question: What extra duties fall on an organisation designated as a Significant Data Fiduciary?
questions.rationale: Appoint a Data Protection Officer based in India and answerable to the board, appoint an independent data auditor, and undertake periodic Data Protection Impact Assessments and audits.
questions.anchor: independent data auditor

questions.question: When must a company delete the personal data it holds?
questions.rationale: Erase upon consent withdrawal or as soon as the specified purpose is no longer served, whichever is earlier, unless retention is required by law — and cause its processors to do the same.
questions.anchor: specified purpose is no longer being served

questions.question: Which security standard is recognised as satisfying the reasonable-security requirement for sensitive personal data?
questions.rationale: IS/ISO/IEC 27001 is named as such a standard, with compliance deemed if certified or audited regularly by an approved independent auditor.
questions.anchor: IS/ISO/IEC 27001

questions.question: Can a company be made to pay damages for a data breach caused by its own poor security?
questions.rationale: A body corporate negligent in maintaining reasonable security practices for sensitive personal data, causing wrongful loss or gain, is liable to pay compensation to the affected person. (Note: the DPDP Act's amendment schedule omits 43A on its commencement; the section stands in this print.)
questions.anchor: negligent in implementing and maintaining reasonable security practices

questions.question: An employee of a service provider leaks customer information they had access to under a services contract. What does the law provide?
questions.rationale: Disclosure of personal information secured while providing contractual services, without consent or in breach of a lawful contract and with intent or knowledge of likely wrongful loss/gain: imprisonment up to three years, fine up to five lakh rupees, or both.
questions.anchor: secured access to any material containing personal information

questions.question: If a contract fixes a penalty amount for breach, can the innocent party recover that full amount automatically?
questions.rationale: The party is entitled only to reasonable compensation not exceeding the named sum or penalty, whether or not actual damage is proved — the stated figure is a ceiling, not an entitlement.
questions.anchor: not exceeding the amount so named

questions.question: Are agreements stopping someone from carrying on their trade or profession enforceable in India?
questions.rationale: Void to that extent, with the sole statutory exception for the seller of a business's goodwill within reasonable local limits.
questions.anchor: restrained from exercising a lawful profession

questions.question: What kinds of losses can the injured party recover when a contract is broken?
questions.rationale: Loss naturally arising in the usual course, or which the parties knew at contracting to be a likely result; no compensation for remote and indirect loss.
questions.anchor: remote and indirect loss

questions.question: For which corporate actions does the board need shareholder approval by special resolution rather than its own resolution?
questions.rationale: Selling or disposing of the whole or substantially the whole of an undertaking, investing compensation from mergers otherwise than in trust securities, borrowing beyond paid-up capital plus free reserves plus securities premium, and remitting a director's debt.
questions.anchor: consent of the company by a special resolution

questions.question: Who can validly sign contracts on behalf of a company?
questions.rationale: Any key managerial personnel, or an officer or employee of the company duly authorised by the Board.
questions.anchor: signed by any key managerial personnel

questions.question: How fast must an online platform deal with a user complaint about content?
questions.rationale: Acknowledge within 24 hours and resolve within 7 days as amended; removal-of-information complaints resolved within 36 hours, and certain individual complaints acted on within 2 hours.
questions.anchor: acknowledge the complaint within twenty-four hours

questions.question: What officers must a large social media platform appoint in India?
questions.rationale: A Chief Compliance Officer resident in India, a nodal contact person for 24x7 law-enforcement coordination, and a Resident Grievance Officer.
questions.anchor: Chief Compliance Officer

questions.question: When does a hosting intermediary lose its immunity for content its users post?
questions.rationale: On conspiring, abetting or aiding the unlawful act, or on failing to expeditiously remove or disable access after actual knowledge or government notification.
questions.anchor: expeditiously remove or disable access

questions.question: What insurance coverage are we, the customer, required to carry under the agreement?
questions.rationale: The MSA imposes no insurance obligation on the customer.
questions.nearby_trap: 10.2 requires the PROVIDER to maintain insurance for its own equipment and facilities — semantically adjacent, answers the opposite question.

questions.question: How much notice must the provider give before increasing prices under the MSA?
questions.rationale: The MSA has no price-increase notice period; pricing is per accepted Purchase Order and changes go through the Change Request process.
questions.nearby_trap: 6.2.1 says provider-initiated non-material changes must not alter agreed pricing — related wording, no notice period.
questions.answered_elsewhere: TOS-leapswitch.pdf section 4 (30 days' notice) — for website terms, not the MSA.

questions.question: Does the MSA let us conduct an on-site audit of the provider's facilities or security practices?
questions.rationale: No customer audit right exists in the MSA.
questions.nearby_trap: 20.4 allows requesting documentation to confirm anti-money-laundering compliance — an audit-flavoured clause that does not grant a facilities or security audit.
questions.answered_elsewhere: TOS-leapswitch.pdf section 10 grants a data-processing audit right on 30 days' notice.

questions.question: Does the MSA prevent us from also buying infrastructure from the provider's competitors?
questions.rationale: No exclusivity or non-compete obligation exists anywhere in the MSA.
questions.nearby_trap: 9.6(c) restricts reselling and misrepresenting affiliation — adjacent to competitive-relationship language without addressing exclusivity.

questions.question: How quickly must support respond to a critical ticket, and is there a credit if they miss it?
questions.rationale: The SLA commits to availability only; no support response-time targets or credits exist in it (the MSA defers response times to 'the applicable SLA', which states none).
questions.nearby_trap: The uptime commitment and service-credit tables — the same remedy vocabulary applied to a different failure.

questions.question: What uptime does the provider commit to for shared web hosting?
questions.rationale: The commitment table covers dedicated servers, power, and public/private network only; shared hosting appears in no uptime table in either SLA.
questions.nearby_trap: The Minimum Uptime table itself — it answers the identical question for five other service categories.

questions.question: How long does the provider promise to take to restore service after an outage begins?
questions.rationale: Neither SLA contains any restoration-time or recovery-time objective; commitments are monthly-percentage based only.
questions.nearby_trap: The Minimum Uptime table — availability percentages read as if they imply a recovery promise, and do not.

questions.question: Does the provider take backups of our hosted data by default, and on what schedule?
questions.rationale: No default backup obligation, schedule or retention exists; backups appear only as a purchasable service name in the definitions and the refunds list.
questions.nearby_trap: Section 10's data-return provision (7-day retrieval window) — about return after termination, not backup during service.

questions.question: What does a dedicated server cost per month?
questions.rationale: No pricing appears in any supplied document; section 2 defers features and pricing to the website and order confirmation.
questions.nearby_trap: Section 4 (Payment Terms) — billing cycles and currencies, no prices.

questions.question: How long is CCTV footage from the datacenters retained?
questions.rationale: Section 12 mentions CCTV monitoring as a physical security measure, but the section 9 retention table has no entry for CCTV footage.
questions.nearby_trap: Section 9's retention table — it answers the identical question for six other data categories.

questions.question: Within how many hours must a Data Fiduciary notify the Data Protection Board of a personal data breach?
questions.rationale: Section 8(6) requires intimation 'in such form and manner as may be prescribed' — the Act itself fixes no time limit; that is left to rules.
questions.nearby_trap: Section 8(6) itself, plus the 6-hour CERT-In deadline that appears in other corpus documents and is about a different regulator.

questions.question: How much compensation can an affected individual claim from a company under the DPDP Act?
questions.rationale: The Act provides monetary penalties credited to the Consolidated Fund of India (sections 33-34); it grants individuals no compensation remedy — and its section 44(2)(a) omits the IT Act provision that did.
questions.nearby_trap: Section 33 and the penalty Schedule — large rupee figures that are fines payable to the state, not damages payable to the individual.
questions.answered_elsewhere: IT_Act_2000.pdf section 43A provides compensation to affected persons (as printed).

questions.question: For how many years must an intermediary preserve user information under section 67C of the IT Act?
questions.rationale: 67C requires preservation 'for such duration... as the Central Government may prescribe' — the Act states no period, only the penalty for contravention (up to three years' imprisonment).
questions.nearby_trap: 67C itself, and the 180-day and 5-year periods in the CERT-In Directions, which arise under a different instrument.
